notable_absence.finding: This page never mentions durability, transactions, or any other concept from the rest of this batch - it is a clean, orthogonal outlier. Despite the batch being otherwise durability/transaction-heavy, compression is documented as a fully independent client-server negotiation concern with its own limits (edition gating, 20MiB size ceiling) and its own tuning surface (CompressionConfig), with zero cross-links to any transaction or durability material anywhere on the page.

cross_component_finding: compression:data-compression (already promoted from a Server-side extraction) is reused wholesale here rather than reinvented - this SDK concept-doc is purely the CLIENT's view of a mechanism whose actual MODE configuration (off/passive/active) lives entirely on the server/bucket side. The SDK's own sdk:compression-config only tunes client-local heuristics (the minSize threshold and the compression ratio) for WHEN to bother attempting compression at all - it has no ability to change the negotiated mode itself.
cross_product_finding: The page's own TIP callout ties its behavior directly to Server-side enforcement rather than to any Java-SDK-specific limit: Couchbase Server itself decompresses an incoming document to validate it and measure it against `max data size` (20 MiB), rejecting oversized documents with an E2BIG 'too big' error code regardless of which SDK sent them - the size ceiling and its enforcement point are both Server properties that this SDK page merely explains the client-side consequence of.
